Panteleimon the Healer

Icons

Saints

St. Panteleimon the Healer

Pantaleon · Panteleemon

What is depictedHistory and traditionPublished explanationSources

The fifteenth-century Byzantine panel depicts the young physician martyr Panteleimon. Its catalogue identifies the Pushkin Museum work.

[1] Displayed work;file-level title,description,date and visual identification

What is depicted

Panteleimon stands in a red garment with a small medical container and a slender instrument. His youthful face and compact pose are preserved within the worn panel. These visible attributes identify the traditional physician depiction without establishing every detail of his later martyrdom narratives.

[1] Displayed work;file-level title,description,date and visual identification

History and tradition

The underlying painting is identified as a fifteenth-century Byzantine work. The file-level reproduction carries a CC BY-SA3.0 record and retains its exact attribution. The object’s medieval date is distinct from the martyr’s life in the early fourth century.

[1] Displayed work;file-level title,description,date and visual identification

Published explanation

Martyr, died about 305. According to legend he was the son of a rich pagan, Eustorgius of Nicomedia, and had been instructed in Christianity by his Christian mother, Eubula. Afterwards he became estranged from Christianity. He studied medicine and became physician to the Emperor Maximianus. He was won back to Christianity by the priest Hermolaus. Upon the death of his father he came into possession of a large fortune. Envious colleagues denounced him to the emperor during the Diocletian persecution. …

Klemens Löffler’s historical1911 Catholic Encyclopedia article. Its opening explicitly identifies the detailed story as legend;that source perspective is preserved.

[2] Article opening,medical background and denunciation

… It was not until he himself desired it that it was possible to behead him.

The same historical author’s account of the received execution story.

[2] Article first paragraph,closing execution sentence
